subject: Regulatory Edge Deployment: Isolation & Operator Access Capability Matrix
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@cedarpointhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Matt Green <mgreen@cloudprocure.io>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up: isolation/operator access details for CedarPoint edge sites

Hi Sergio / Laura,

Thanks again for the overview last week. Procurement and our security engineering leads reviewed the high-level deck and flagged a few required details for our formal RFP. We need a capability matrix that maps Redwood's controls to our regulatory checklist for on-prem / VPC / sealed-edge deployments. Specifically we need:

- Operator access model (human operator vs. sealed operator) and how credentials are managed and rotated
- KMS/HSM integration options and whether key material ever leaves the customer boundary
- Network egress controls and preferred topologies for air-gapped sites
- Evidence references (SOC2, vulnerability scan cadence) and any available network diagrams

Can you send a completed matrix and any supporting evidence by EOD Wednesday PDT? Also include a short note about your recommended minimal operator profile for our on-site staff.

We may loop in legal for contract language once we validate capabilities. Matt is helping us coordinate cloud purchase and will attach a procurement checklist.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this will determine whether we progress to a PoC.

Regards,
Anika Rao
Sr. Procurement Manager
CedarPoint Health

[Attachment: procurement-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood-inference.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@cedarpointhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com>, Matt Green <mgreen@cloudprocure.io>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: isolation/operator access details for CedarPoint edge sites

Anika — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a preliminary isolation & operator-access matrix that maps Redwood controls to common regulatory checkpoints. Highlights up front:

- Operator access: we support three operator models (remote-vetted, customer-on-site operator, sealed-operator with ephemeral credentials). By default for air-gapped installs we recommend the sealed-operator model to minimize persistent credentials on the appliance.
- Keys: KHSM/KMS integration supported. Customer-managed keys (via external KMS or HSM) are supported and can be configured such that key material never leaves the HSM-protected module. We list supported partners and config notes in the matrix.
- Egress: default is 'no outbound' for sealed installs; optional controlled egress over customer breakout with allowlist and TLS pinning for telemetry.

Next steps I propose: 1) review the attached matrix, 2) highlight any rows where you need vendor evidence (we will attach SOC2 excerpt and a redacted network diagram), 3) set a technical workshop with our solutions engineering team (30–45m).

Attached: isolation-capability-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — I can revise the matrix after your feedback.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: isolation/operator access details for CedarPoint edge sites

Sergio — reviewed quickly with our security engineering lead (cc'd Marcus). Quick clarifications before we take this to legal: 

- Sealed-operator model sounds promising. Can you confirm whether sealed-operator flows require any outbound connection during operator session establishment? We need to ensure no key or session material is routed via Redwood-managed tenants.
- For KMS: is Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) supported with HSM-backed keys on-prem, and do you provide an HSM connector bundle or is that customer-delivered?
- Evidence: the SOC2 excerpt will be sufficient for initial review; we will need a signed attestation for patch cadence and vulnerability scanning during contract stage.

Also, can you include a one-page runbook (operator minimal steps) — our ops team wants to understand expected human intervention during upgrade and incident recovery.

Thanks — if you can confirm by EOD Tuesday PT we can get legal to draft the reciprocal language for the PoC SOW.

Regards,
Anika

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: isolation/operator access details for CedarPoint edge sites

Anika / Marcus — thanks for the targeted questions. Short answers below, and I attached the SOC2 excerpt and a redacted network diagram for your team.

- Sealed-operator session establishment: sealed-operator requires an outbound-only authenticated handshake to the customer-designated mediation endpoint (customer-owned). No operator credentials or keys are stored in Redwood-managed tenants. Session tokens are ephemeral (TTL < 15 minutes) and derived from customer-managed attestations.

- BYOK with HSM: yes — we support BYOK. For on-prem HSM usage we ship a small connector package (signed binary + configuration) or, if you prefer, we can provide an integration spec and your engineering team can implement the connector. When using customer HSMs, key material never leaves the HSM.

- Runbook: attached is a 1-page operator runbook (embedded in the matrix tab) that covers upgrade steps, emergency rollback, and incident escalation contacts. Minimal operator profile:
  - Level 1: operator with restricted CLI access for start/stop and patch apply (no key management)
  - Level 2: operator with key attestation permission (requires 2-person approval for HSM ops)

Attached: SOC2-TypeII-summary.pdf, network-diagram-v2.png

Next: happy to run the 45-minute technical workshop Thursday or Friday (I'll propose times). I'll also drop the NDA/DocuSign link to the Drive folder for any confidential artifacts we need to exchange.

Best,
—Sergio

Redwood Inference
